newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open firmer.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open firmer.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were seen opening slightly higher Monday, in line with LME copper prices, as the market continued its recovery from oversold levels, following a plunge caused by fund long liquidation early last week.
COMEX September copper was seen opening unchanged to up 0.50 cent from Friday's close at 111.85 cents, after trading between 111.50 and 113.50 cents in overnight ACCESS trade.
COMEX copper prices fell more than 10 cents early last week week, retreating from 12 month highs, before finding some support.
LME copper stocks rose 250 tonnes Monday to 125,150 tonnes, while COMEX stocks fell 817 short tons Friday to 47,748 short tons.
In industry news, Chile's El Teniente mine, owned by Codelco, is working at 60 percent of capacity, as damage caused by heavy snowfall at the weekend is repaired.
The mine, Codelco's second largest pit, expects to return to normal output by Tuesday. El Teniente produced 345,000 tonnes of fine copper in 1996.

Meanwhile, union representatives said Saturday that striking workers at Inco's Sudbury operation in Canada had voted 80 percent in favor of accepting a labor deal to end a four week strike. The Sudbury mine produces about 200 million pounds of copper annually and supplies the U.S. North East.
In other news, Broken Hill Pty Ltd's (BHP) said Monday it was resuming shipments of copper concentrates from its OK Tedi mine in Papau New Guinea following heavy rains over the weekend.
